title: Ball-in-Hand Conditioning Circuit
description: A conditioning circuit that keeps a ball in hand throughout — dribble sprints, defensive slides with a ball, and finishing layups under fatigue.

content.objective: Build conditioning that transfers directly to the game by keeping a ball in hand the whole time.
content.setup: A player starts under the basket with a ball and a clear full-court lane.
instructions: Dribble-sprint the length of the court and finish a layup.
Dribble back the other way at a controlled pace, practising a change of direction.
Repeat for a set number of full-court trips without resting the ball.
Finish the circuit with ten free throws to measure composure under fatigue.
coachingPoints: Keep the dribble under control even at top conditioning effort.
Use correct footwork on every finish, not a rushed layup.
Measure the free-throw percentage at the end as a composure check.
commonMistakes: Losing control of the ball by sprinting faster than the handle allows.
Rushing the finishing footwork because of fatigue.
Pacing too conservatively instead of working at real effort.
content.safety: Make sure the full-court lane is clear of other groups before starting.
